name: AML compliance kit for used-car lots and vehicle importers/consignors (Res 196/2020: manual, compliance officer, KYC, ROS, negative reports, annual evaluation, external audit)
buyer: Used-car lots (playas), vehicle importers and consignors, mostly small owner-run businesses. SEPRELAD counted 1,142 lots in 2019. Only 110 belong to the CIVU association.
trigger: SEPRELAD Res 196 of 4 Sept 2020 (Ferrere). Obligations: AML/CFT manual and code of ethics; compliance officer (the owner may fill it in a sole proprietorship); KYC with a simplified route up to 15 minimum wages; ROS; negative report if no ROS in 3 months; risk assessment every 2 years; annual evaluation reported to SEPRELAD within 90 days of fiscal year end; external audit report within 180 days. The USD 10,000 threshold from Res 85/15 was removed.
evidence: https://ferrere.com/es/novedades/nuevo-reglamento-de-prevencion-de-lavado-de-activos-y-financiamiento-del-terrorismo-para-personas-fisicas-o-juridicas-involucrad/ (Res 196 contents, fetched). https://www.ultimahora.com/seprelad-el-50-playa-autos-eluden-el-control-antilavado-n2852685.html (fetched; the article is dated 2 Nov 2019, not 2026: 1,142 lots, 704 warned, under 50% file ROS, sanctions announced). https://www.lanacion.com.py/negocios/2021/02/12/seprelad-instruye-en-reporte-de-operaciones-al-sector-automotriz/ (SEPRELAD instructivo, SIRO system, seen in snippet only). Competitor search found no software vendor or SEPRELAD-approved product for dealer AML.
existing: Competitor search 'software ROS SEPRELAD playas de autos concesionarias sistema cumplimiento antilavado Paraguay' found no vendor. SEPRELAD's own SIRO/ROS-WEB reporting portal exists (free state tool, role for forms not checked). General law-firm and consultant compliance services are likely but not seen.
unchecked: Current count of lots; whether SIRO already offers templates for the manual, annual evaluation and negative report; enforcement and fines since 2020; whether the sector is small enough that consultants already serve it; the price buyers would pay. Also whether CADAM/CIVU already supply a template.

first_check.duty: SEPRELAD Res 196 of 4 Sept 2020 is the AML/CFT rule for anyone importing, buying, selling or consigning motor vehicles, under Law 1015/97 as amended by Law 3783/09. It replaced Res 85/15. Última Hora dates the rule to 9 Sept 2020 (article fetched). It requires: a full AML/CFT prevention system with a manual and a code of ethics, a compliance officer, customer KYC with risk profiles and monitoring (a simplified route up to 15 minimum wages for single payments and 20 for instalment sales), suspicious-transaction reports (ROS) filed through SEPRELAD's SIRO system, a risk assessment at least every 2 years, an annual compliance-officer report due within 90 days of fiscal year end, and an external audit report due within 180 days. I found no repeal or replacement for 2024-2026, but I did not see the official text and did not confirm that the rule is still in force. I could not confirm the specific fines or any enforcement since 2020. The 2019 article mentions warnings to 704 firms and sanctions being announced.
first_check.market: Última Hora (2 Nov 2019) counted 1,142 used-car lots, of which 704 were warned and fewer than half filed ROS. Only 110 lots belong to CIVU. Another article in the same period says more than 700 firms and individuals own used-car lots, plus the CADAM importers (over 90 brands). I found no current register count. Roughly 700-1,200 obligated businesses, many informal.
first_check.competitor: I found no vendor offering a full AML kit (manual, risk matrix, KYC files, ROS and negative reports, annual report, audit preparation) for car lots. Partial overlap: Compliance Paraguay, a local consultancy (La Nación, Aug 2024), sells a database of more than 9,000 politically exposed persons and explicitly targets car dealerships among other obligated firms. It is a screening-only tool, and the article does not say whether it handles manuals, ROS or annual reports. SEPRELAD's SIRO is a free state tool, but only for filing reports. Two other offers were seen but not checked: certification courses that train compliance officers (FOTRIEM/BNF) and law-firm advisory work (Ferrere). Neither CADAM nor CIVU templates were found.
first_check.reason: The duty is real, recurring (annual report, external audit, ROS and negative reports, risk review every 2 years) and specific to this sector. I found no tool that does the whole compliance job. Compliance Paraguay sells only a database for screening politically exposed persons, and SIRO is only for filing. Against it: there are only about 700-1,200 buyers, many of them informal and below half compliant. I could not confirm fines or current enforcement, so how much they would pay is uncertain. The external audit is a separate outside cost, and law firms and consultants probably already sell manuals. An MVP is simple (template manual, KYC forms, report calendar, risk matrix) and could later extend to other obligated firms without a sector supervisor (real estate, pawnshops, jewellers). Reachable through CIVU and CADAM.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The partial overlaps are SEPRELAD's free SIRO portal (filing only), generic PEP and sanctions screening APIs (Didit, TheKYB), and consultancies such as Compliance Paraguay that sell a PEP database. None of them covers the whole Res 196 workflow.
challenge_check.reason: I found nothing that kills it. No Paraguayan vendor sells a full Res 196 kit for car lots (manual, risk assessment, KYC files, ROS and negative-report calendar, annual evaluation). SEPRELAD's free SIRO only takes ROS and negative-report filings; vehicle importers were added in 2023 (search snippet). Global screening APIs such as Didit and TheKYB cover PEP and sanctions checks only. I found no repeal of Res 196 and no newer rule replacing it. Three things weaken it. Enforcement found so far is warnings, not fines: 704 lots warned, per the 2019 article. Most of the roughly 1,142 lots are informal (only 110 belong to CIVU). And law firms or consultants (Ferrere, Compliance Paraguay) probably sell one-off manuals. Willingness to pay is not verified.
